t270.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿī, Abū ʿImrān al-Kūfī the jurist, trustworthy but frequently sends, of the fifth generation, who died in year 96 aged about fifty.
as: Trustworthy, except that he frequently sends (mursal).
لم يحدث عن أحد من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد أدرك منهم جماعة
He narrated from none of the Prophet's Companions though he met a number of them.
وكان رجلا صالحا فقيها متوقيا قليل التكلف
He was a righteous man, a jurist, cautious and free of affectation.
Ibrāhīm was an assayer of hadith (expert at telling sound from unsound).
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
مراسيل إبراهيم أحب إلي من مراسيل الشعبي
I prefer Ibrāhīm's mursal reports to those of al-Shaʿbī.
أما إنه ما ترك أحدا أعلم منه أو أفقه منه
He left behind no one more knowledgeable or more learned in law than he.
سعيد بن جبير, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
Do you ask me for fatwas while Ibrāhīm is among you?
ما ذكرت لإبراهيم حديثا قط إلا زادني فيه
I never mentioned a hadith to Ibrāhīm without his adding to it for me.
We held Ibrāhīm in awe as one holds a governor.
ما بالكوفة أعجب إلي من إبراهيم وخيثمة
There is no one in Kufa I admire more than Ibrāhīm and Khaythamah.
ابن عون, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
By God, he left no one like him after him.
Ibrāhīm dead is more learned in law than he is alive.

t384.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr ibn Bahrām al-Kawsaj, Abū Yaʿqūb al-Tamīmī al-Marwazī, as trustworthy and firmly established, of the eleventh generation, who died in the year fifty-one.
as: ثقة مأمون، أحد الأئمة من أصحاب الحديث.
Trustworthy and dependable, one of the leading hadith scholars.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
الحاكم أبو عبد الله, quoted by al-Mizzī
وهو أحد الأئمة من أصحاب الحديث، من الزهاد والمتمسكين بالسنة
He was one of the leading authorities in hadith, among the ascetics and those who held to the Sunnah.
كان فقيها عالما، وهو الذي دون عن أحمد بن حنبل وإسحاق بن راهويه المسائل
He was a learned jurist and compiled the legal questions from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh.

t8391.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says Abū al-Malīḥ al-Fārisī al-Madanī al-Kharrāṭ, named Ṣubayḥ (or Ḥumayd), is trustworthy, of the seventh generation.

t8467.bio: Ibn Abī Khuzāmah transmits from his father, or it is said from Abū Khuzāmah from his father, which is correct; he is unknown and of the third generation.

t977.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jundub al-Khayr al-Azdī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, killer of the sorcerer, with disagreement over his Companionship; Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among trustworthy Successors, and Abū ʿUbaydah said he was killed at Ṣiffīn.
